theatres.name: Iran / Strait of Hormuz
theatres.status_label: Ceasefire declared 'OVER' by Trump, then walked back the same day; largest post-MOU strike wave stays AIR/MARITIME — ground rung unchanged — July 9: DAY 133 / CEASEFIRE 'OVER' (RHETORICALLY) / BLOCKADE LIFTED DAY 21. On July 8 US CENTCOM announced 'additional strikes' (aggregating to 80+ targets and 60+ IRGC small boats plus air-defense, C2, coastal-radar, surveillance and anti-ship-missile sites), and Trump, at the NATO Ankara summit, declared the ceasefire and MOU 'over' ('a waste of time'; Iran 'vicious, violent'; 'every time they hit us, we hit them 20') and threatened to bomb/blockade Iran again — then walked it back hours later ('I don't think it's going to start again'). Brent settled +5.2% at $78.02/bbl (eased on the walk-back). Even at this rhetorical peak the exchange stayed AIR and MARITIME — no US troops in Iran, no Kharg assault, no new ARG/MEU order, no draft; blockade lifted (Day 21). Khamenei was buried at Mashhad's Imam Reza shrine July 9, closing the state funeral; new Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei still absent. The imminent-ground-invasion / Hormuz-and-Kharg-seizure thesis stays disconfirmed-and-inverted — Iran, not the US, is using force at the chokepoint. || Kinetic cycle RESUMES — Iran attacks three tankers, US answers with air strikes and an oil-waiver revocation; ground rung still unchanged — July 8: DAY 132 / CEASEFIRE DAY 92 (BREACHED) / BLOCKADE LIFTED DAY 20. The five-day off-the-kinetic streak broke on July 7: Iran's IRGC attacked three tankers near Hormuz (Qatari LNG carrier Al-Rekayyat, Saudi supertanker Wedyan, and a drone-hit tanker) to enforce its 'designated routes'; US CENTCOM launched 'a series of powerful strikes' (its largest post-MOU package) on air-defense, coastal, SAM, anti-ship-cruise-missile, drone and port sites near Bandar Abbas/Qeshm/Bandar Khamir/Sirik; and OFAC revoked Iran's oil-sales waiver (wind-down July 17). Iran called it a 'blatant violation' of the MOU and vowed 'decisive actions'; talks stay paused for the funeral week. Brent spiked ~5.5% to ~$76/bbl. The exchange stayed AIR and MARITIME — no US troops in Iran, no Kharg assault, no new ARG/MEU order, no draft; blockade lifted (Day 20). Khamenei's funeral crossed into Iraq (Najaf/Karbala July 8) ahead of burial at Mashhad July 9; new Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei still absent. The imminent-ground-invasion / Hormuz-and-Kharg-seizure thesis stays disconfirmed-and-inverted — Iran, not the US, is using force at the chokepoint. || Funeral rites move to Qom; US talks stay paused; Hormuz governed by negotiation and Iranian toll claims — July 7: DAY 131 / CEASEFIRE DAY 91 / BLOCKADE LIFTED DAY 19. The war ran a fifth straight day off the kinetic track. After the July 6 main Tehran procession (projected up to 20 million mourners), the cortege for slain Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei reached Qom (Jamkaran mosque, Fatima Masoumeh shrine) on July 7, ahead of Najaf/Karbala July 8 and burial at the Imam Reza shrine in Mashhad July 9. New Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei (named March 9) still had not appeared publicly — reporting now ties his absence both to an Israeli assassination threat and to Feb 28 strike injuries (US officials earlier: 'wounded and likely disfigured') — keeping the who-runs-Iran question live. US-Iran talks stayed paused for the funeral week (Doha round: 'positive progress,' no breakthrough). On Hormuz, Iran maintained mid-August transit 'service fees' (US rejects) and the UK/France backed an Oman-led free-navigation effort. Brent held near pre-war ~$72/bbl (Saudi exports ~90% of pre-war, UAE >3.9M bpd, total Hormuz flows >10M bpd). No new strikes or shipping incidents reported. The ground rung stayed unchanged and de-escalatory — no US troops in Iran, no Kharg assault, no new ARG/MEU order, no draft; blockade lifted (Day 19). || Main funeral day; US talks stay paused; Hormuz governed by negotiation and Iranian toll claims — July 6: DAY 130 / CEASEFIRE DAY 90 / BLOCKADE LIFTED DAY 18. The war stayed off the kinetic track on the central and largest day of Khamenei's six-day state funeral (main Tehran procession Imam Hossein Sq. to Azadi Sq. at 6 a.m. local; Tehran's mayor projected up to 20 million mourners — potentially the city's largest-ever gathering; rites continue to Qom July 7, Najaf July 8, burial in Mashhad July 9). New Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei (named March 9) still had not appeared publicly, keeping the succession/who-runs-Iran question live. US-Iran talks stayed paused for the funeral week (to resume 'at the earliest possible time' per Qatar). On Hormuz, Iran's ambassador to China reaffirmed mid-August transit 'service fees' (with 'special treatment' for friendly nations; US rejects), Iran warned against a 'military display of extra-regional powers,' and the UK/France backed Oman on free navigation. OPEC+ agreed July 5 to raise August output by 188,000 bpd; oil markets reopened July 6 with Brent near pre-war ~$72/bbl (Saudi exports ~90% of pre-war, UAE >3.9M bpd, total Hormuz flows >10M bpd). The ground rung stayed unchanged and de-escalatory on the US side — no US troops in Iran, no Kharg assault, no new ARG/MEU order, no draft; blockade lifted (Day 18). Israel renewed a threat to kill Iran's new supreme leader. No new strikes or shipping incidents July 5-6. The imminent-ground-invasion / Hormuz-and-Kharg-seizure thesis stays disconfirmed-and-inverted; live risks are deal durability (post-funeral round) and Hormuz governance (mid-August toll deadline). || Second funeral day; US talks stay paused; a succession question sharpens; Hormuz contest runs on — July 5: DAY 129 / CEASEFIRE DAY 89 / BLOCKADE LIFTED DAY 17. The war stayed off the kinetic track through a second day of Khamenei's six-day state funeral (Tehran lying-in-state; Qom procession July 5; 15-20 million mourners projected, the largest in Iranian history; delegations from 70+ countries incl. Russia's Medvedev, Pakistan's PM Sharif, Iraq's leaders, the Afghan Taliban FM, Hamas and Hezbollah — but no high-level GCC and no Western invitees). CNN reported the whereabouts of the new Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei (named March 9) remain unknown, sharpening a succession/who-runs-Iran question. US-Iran talks stayed paused for the funeral week; on Hormuz, Iran's deputy FM issued a 'serious warning' to France and the UK over their naval movements and reaffirmed mid-August 'service fees,' while the UK and France pledged to work with Oman on 'safe transit for ships of all nations.' Oil markets were closed (US Independence-Day weekend; last print Brent ~$72/bbl, July 3; Saudi/UAE exports ~90% of pre-war). The ground rung stayed de-escalatory on the US side — no US troops in Iran, no Kharg assault, no new ARG/MEU order, no draft; blockade lifted (Day 17). No new strikes or shipping incidents July 4-5. The imminent-ground-invasion / Hormuz-and-Kharg-seizure thesis stays disconfirmed-and-inverted; live risks are deal durability (post-funeral round) and Hormuz governance (mid-August toll deadline). || War moves OFF the kinetic track and into a paused negotiation plus a state funeral — July 4: the two-day Doha round (indirect, via Qatar and Pakistan) concluded July 2 with 'positive progress' but NO breakthrough (a frozen-asset goods-purchase channel, a violations-deconfliction line, a Hormuz-passage focus), while the core disputes stayed open (US rejects any Iranian-led toll mechanism; Tehran asserts joint Iran-Oman sovereignty and plans tolls from mid-August; no frozen funds moved; Ghalibaf denied IAEA access to the bombed Fordow/Natanz/Isfahan sites). The US then agreed to halt talks for a week as Iran opened a SIX-DAY STATE FUNERAL for slain Supreme Leader Khamenei (July 4-9, Tehran→Qom→Najaf/Karbala→Mashhad; 15-20 million mourners expected — the largest in Iranian history; ~30 delegations incl. Russia's Medvedev and China) — DAY 128 / CEASEFIRE DAY 88 / BLOCKADE LIFTED DAY 16. Oil at a four-month low (Brent ~$71.5/bbl; Trump: 'they've come a long way'); Hormuz traffic recovering (258 vessels/week, up from 138). Iran, not the US, is asserting coercive Strait control (Tehran-designated tanker routes, a 'forceful response' threat, mid-August tolls) — the inverse of a US seizure. Still off the ground rung and de-escalatory on the US side: no US troops in Iran, no Kharg assault, no new ARG/MEU, no draft; USS Boxer ARG disaggregated. The imminent-ground-invasion / Hormuz-and-Kharg-seizure thesis stays disconfirmed-and-inverted; the live risk is deal durability — now whether the post-funeral round convenes and whether the toll and inspection disputes are bridged. || Breach-retaliation cycle BREAKS into a stand-down — June 29: the US and Iran agree to halt mutual attacks and let vessels move freely through Hormuz, and Trump announces a fresh high-level meeting in Doha on Tuesday June 30 (Witkoff and Kushner attending; topic re-scoped to the Hormuz standoff), even as Iran's deputy FM Gharibabadi denies any technical talks were scheduled — DAY 124 / CEASEFIRE DAY 84 / BLOCKADE LIFTED DAY 12. Iran-Oman open a first Strait-management meeting (demining/tolls disputed); Iran receives $6B of $12B in frozen assets; oil eases toward a four-month low (~$69.70/bbl). Still off the ground rung and de-escalatory on the US side: blockade lifted, USS Boxer ARG disaggregated, Strait reopening by negotiation. The imminent-ground-invasion / Hormuz-and-Kharg-seizure thesis stays disconfirmed-and-inverted; the live risk is deal durability — now whether the Doha meeting actually convenes.
theatres.summary: JUNE 30 (Day 124): The three-day breach-retaliation cycle broke. On June 29 a US official said the US and Iran agreed to stand down and let vessels move freely through Hormuz, and Trump announced a fresh high-level meeting in Doha on Tuesday June 30 (Witkoff and Kushner attending; talks moved from Switzerland and re-scoped to the Hormuz standoff), while Iran's deputy FM Gharibabadi denied any technical talks had been scheduled. Iran and Oman held a first Strait-management meeting (demining and tolls disputed; Iran insists on demining alone and rejects a France-Oman initiative; Oman/GCC reject tolls as 'not acceptable'); Iran received $6B of $12B in frozen Qatari-held assets under the MOU (reportedly earmarked for US wheat and corn). Oil eased: Brent rose only slightly to ~$69.70/bbl off a four-month low. Hormuz traffic stayed thinned (29 vessels Sat, 12 Sun, down from 70 Wed) but container lines resumed Gulf services. The ground rung was unchanged and de-escalatory on the US side — the day's US move was diplomatic, not a ground operation; no US troops in Iran, no Kharg assault, no new ARG/MEU order, no draft; blockade lifted (Day 12), USS Boxer ARG disaggregated. (NPR; CNBC; NBC News; CBS News; Euronews; The National; TradingEconomics, June 29, 2026.)

theatres.status_label: JULY 8-9 — NATO ANKARA SUMMIT CONCLUDES; UKRAINE'S DEEP-STRIKE CAMPAIGN CONTINUES: The Ankara summit (July 7-8) closed with a push for a 5% defense-spending goal and continued Ukraine support; Zelensky met Trump bilaterally (pressing for Patriots and interceptors) and Germany is financing two Patriot systems. Notably, no new US ground-deployment surge was announced — and the Pentagon's European force-posture review may DRAW DOWN US forces in Eastern Europe (no rotational brigade retained in Romania). On July 8 Ukrainian drones struck Russia's Saratov oil refinery and a Tatarstan petrochemical plant, hit 9 tankers in the Sea of Azov, and struck a Voronezh air base (Su-34/Su-35); Russia cut Kerch Bridge rail service (11 of 18 routes cancelled from July 8). The Kremlin continues to reject direct negotiations. Kostiantynivka stays contested; Russia holds ~20% with no confirmed net change. || JULY 7-8 — NATO ANKARA SUMMIT: allies confirmed €70B ($80B) in 2026 Ukraine military aid (largely repackaged existing NATO/EU funding) and a goal of at least an equivalent 2027 level; Trump and Zelensky met bilaterally, with Zelensky pressing for Patriot systems and interceptor missiles after the July 6 Russian barrage on the Kyiv region killed ~22 (15 in Kyiv city) and injured ~90. Germany is financing two Patriot systems. Kostiantynivka stayed contested — Russia's July 3 'liberation' claim disputed by Kyiv; ISW assesses small-group infiltration, not consolidated control. Russia holds ~20% with no confirmed net change. No US ground-deployment surge. || JULY 6-7 — UKRAINE'S DEEPEST STRIKE OF THE WAR (OMSK); RUSSIA'S MASS BARRAGE ON KYIV; TRUMP-PUTIN CALL AHEAD OF ANKARA NATO SUMMIT: On July 6 Ukrainian drones struck the Omsk refinery — Russia's largest, ~2,500-3,000 km away — the deepest strike of the full-scale war (also Yaroslavl/Slavneft-Yanos and Ust-Luga). Russia answered with a mass overnight barrage on Kyiv (~351 drones + 68 missiles) that killed ~22 and injured ~90 nationwide (15 killed in Kyiv city). Trump held a ~90-min call with Putin ('businesslike and very constructive') and spoke with Zelensky ahead of the NATO summit in Ankara (July 7-8), where he was set to meet Zelensky and Germany is financing two Patriot systems. Kostiantynivka stays contested — Russia proposed a local ceasefire (Ukraine rejected it) and ISW puts Russian presence at ~37% of the city (~4.3% of Lyman), calling Putin's 96% claim 'greatly exaggerated.' Russia holds ~20% with no confirmed net change. No US ground-deployment surge. || JULY 5-6 — KOSTIANTYNIVKA CONTROL STILL CONTESTED; DEEP-STRIKE WAR CONTINUES: Russia's July 3 claim (Gerasimov to Putin) that it had 'liberated' Kostiantynivka stayed disputed — Ukraine's 19th Army Corps commander Madyar reported pushing Russian infiltrators back out at a ~3:53 loss ratio, and ISW/DeepState still assess small-group infiltration, not consolidated control (DeepState: ~12 sq mi net Russian gain over the four weeks to June 23). Ukraine kept up its refinery campaign (Lukoil-Nizhegorodorgsintez, Russia's 4th-largest, halted after a July 2 strike; Ufa hit twice in a week; St. Petersburg oil terminal / Kronstadt July 4; 8 of Russia's top 10 refineries hit in 2026). Russia pressed mass strikes on Kyiv (the July 1-2 barrage killed at least 17-31). After a ~40-min July 4 Zelensky-Trump call, Zelensky pressed allies to accelerate Patriot deliveries and warned of another large-scale Russian attack; talks stay stalled (Putin insists on the 2022 Istanbul Protocols); Russia holds ~20% with no confirmed net change. No US ground-deployment surge. || JULY 4-5 — KOSTIANTYNIVKA CONTROL CONTESTED: Russia's Gerasimov told Putin (July 3) that Russian forces had 'liberated' Kostiantynivka and were closing on Lyman, and Putin hailed it; on July 4 Zelensky and Ukraine's General Staff flatly denied it ('another Russian lie'), with Zelensky challenging Putin to meet him there, and ISW assessed NO confirmed advances July 3 (gains still small-group infiltration, not consolidated control). Pokrovsk stayed heaviest (22 assaults repelled; 268 combat engagements July 3). Ukraine struck the St. Petersburg Oil Terminal and Kronstadt (July 4, ~1,100 km — among the deepest strikes on Putin's home city; 8 of Russia's top 10 refineries hit in 2026). Russia kept up mass strikes (overnight attacks injured ~23 in Kyiv; a July 4 drone hit a Poltava gas facility; after the July 1-2 Kyiv barrage of 74 missiles + 496 drones killed 20-31). A ~40-min Zelensky-Trump call (July 4, 'the best conversation in all this time') agreed to strengthen air defenses and expand joint drone/weapons production, days after a US DoD pause on Patriot and precision-artillery shipments; Zelensky named Patriots his top priority with Merz. Talks stay stalled (Putin still insists on the 2022 Istanbul Protocols); Russia holds ~20% with no confirmed net change; a think-tank estimate put total war casualties above 2 million (up to 600,000 deaths). No US ground-deployment surge. || JULY 1 — WAR REPORT CARD: peace talks remain ON HOLD but the US, Ukraine and Europe 'appear ready to restart negotiations,' while Putin reiterates Russia's original aims — negotiating only on the basis of the 2022 Istanbul Protocols (terms amounting to Ukrainian capitulation). Polling shifts toward a deal: ~60% of Russians support peace negotiations and ~66% of Ukrainians want the government to seek an end to the war as soon as possible. On the ground, KOSTIANTYNIVKA stays Russia's main Donbas effort but gains are limited to small-group infiltration with NO consolidated control — Ukraine's tactical situation is deteriorating and Ukrainian forces are counterattacking; the Russian MoD and Putin are 'falsely framing' the city's seizure as imminent. (Russia Matters/ISW, July 1, 2026.) || JUNE 21 — UKRAINE EXTENDS ITS RUSSIAN-ENERGY STRIKE CAMPAIGN: after the June 18 strike on Moscow's Kapotnya (Moscow Oil) refinery — the largest attack on the capital since 2022 — Ukraine struck a CRIMEAN OIL TERMINAL OVERNIGHT JUNE 21. On the ground, KOSTIANTYNIVKA is now Russia's main objective (Russian forces entered its NE part, tactical breakthrough in the west). Formal peace talks remain FROZEN. || JUNE 5-6: Lavrov reaffirmed the April 2022 Istanbul draft as Moscow's basis for any settlement (Russia as 'guarantor state,' veto over responses to future aggression, strict Ukrainian neutrality/force limits); Russia still claims full Luhansk (Kyiv denies). Over the past year Russia netted +1,427 sq mi (~0.6% of Ukraine) but recorded a net territorial LOSS in April 2026; next Istanbul round proposed June 20-30. — PRIOR: JUNE 4-5: Russia maintains its claim of full control over Luhansk oblast (Kyiv's Joint Forces denies it, citing no changes there) ahead of US-envoy talks; theatres.summary: [JUNE 15-16 UPDATE] Mid-June: the war continued with no breakthrough. Ukrainian drone strikes hit St. Petersburg on June 12 (smoke over the city) as Putin spoke at Russia's flagship economic forum; on June 15 Putin reiterated that any negotiations must happen on Moscow's terms, with his war aims unchanged. Heavy fighting continued on the Pokrovsk and Huliaipole sectors; Ukraine still holds ~80% of its territory (~20% occupied). The theatre keeps stressing US bandwidth but has triggered no US ground-deployment surge. (Kyiv Independent; Critical Threats / ISW, June 12-15, 2026.) [JUNE 5-6] FM Sergei Lavrov reaffirmed Moscow's insistence on the April 2022 Istanbul draft as the basis for a settlement — Russia as a 'guarantor state' with veto power over responses to future aggression and strict neutrality/force caps on Ukraine. Russia maintained its claim of full control over Luhansk oblast (Kyiv denied any change). Over June 2025–June 2026 Russia made a net gain of 1,427 sq mi (~0.6% of Ukraine) but recorded a net LOSS in April 2026; Ukrainian drones killed/incapacitated 35,200+ Russian troops in April, the fifth straight month Moscow's losses outran mobilization. The next direct round is proposed for June 20-30. (Russia Matters; Kyiv Independent, June 2026). [JUNE 3-4] Russia claimed full control of Luhansk oblast (Kyiv denied) ahead of US-envoy talks; fighting continued in the Pokrovsk sector. Following the brief June 2 Istanbul round (a 1,000-1,200 POW swap, a 6,000-body exchange and a wounded-exchange commission, but no ceasefire), Ukraine proposed the next round for June 20-30. (PBS NewsHour; Kyiv Independent; Wikipedia, June 2-4, 2026.) || [JUNE 2] The second direct Russia-Ukraine round in Istanbul ended in under an hour: the sides agreed a new prisoner exchange of at least 1,000 (possibly 1,200) each, a 6,000-body swap, and a commission for seriously wounded troops, but no ceasefire — Russia offered only a 2-3 day pause to retrieve the dead (Zelensky criticized) and Ukraine proposed the next round for June 20-30. An EU summit draft said the bloc was ready to 'step up' but a 'ceasefire must come first.' (Kyiv Independent; PBS NewsHour; Euronews, June 2, 2026). [JUNE 2] A second direct round was held in Istanbul: both sides exchanged memoranda and agreed a new prisoner swap but reached no ceasefire and stayed far apart — Russia seeking recognition of annexed regions and Ukrainian withdrawal within 30 days, Ukraine seeking a full ceasefire, an all-for-all POW exchange, the return of abducted children, and a NATO/EU path; the Pokrovsk sector remained heaviest. (Kyiv Independent; RFE/RL, June 2, 2026). [MAY 31-JUNE 1] A second direct round of talks remained expected around June 2; the Pokrovsk sector stayed the heaviest along the front, with Russia still unable to advance significantly west of Pokrovsk/Myrnohrad and both sides claiming frontline progress. [MAY 30-31] A second direct round of talks remains expected ~June 2; the Pokrovsk sector stays the heaviest along the front, with Russia unable to advance significantly west of Pokrovsk/Myrnohrad since December 2025. POW/humanitarian exchanges continue. MAY 17: Istanbul aftermath — both sides remain far apart on the key conditions for stopping the war; senior officials' comments indicate no convergence. The agreed 1,000-for-1,000 POW exchange proceeds; a second round of direct talks is expected ~June 2 with each side to table a memorandum of its peace terms; Trump continues to press for a direct Putin meeting. PRIOR MAY 16: First direct Russia-Ukraine Istanbul talks in 3 years CONCLUDED after <2 hours — NO ceasefire. Russia (delegation led by Vladimir Medinsky) demanded Ukraine fully withdraw from Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia, Kherson (areas Russia does not fully control); Ukraine (delegation led by Defense Minister Rustem Umerov) offered an immediate full/unconditional 30-day ceasefire, an all-for-all POW exchange, and a Zelensky-Putin meeting. Outcome: a 1,000-for-1,000 POW exchange agreed; each side to present its ceasefire vision in detail; Ukraine handed over a list of forcibly deported children; Kyiv needs ~a week to review and proposed further talks June 20-30; Trump called for a direct Putin meeting. || PRIOR: MAY 15: FIRST DIRECT RUSSIA-UKRAINE ISTANBUL TALKS IN 3 YEARS (delegations: Russia led by Vladimir Medinsky; Ukraine led by Defense Minister Rustem Umerov). Per Kyiv Independent + The Hill + RFE/RL + Newsweek + Wikipedia peace negotiations + Meduza: talks lasted less than 2 hours; produced 1,000-for-1,000 prisoner-of-war exchange agreement but NO ceasefire agreement. Moscow demanded Kyiv completely withdraw from four oblasts Putin claims to have annexed: Donetsk, Luhansk, Zaporizhzhia, Kherson. Kyiv insisted on 'full and unconditional ceasefire' for at least 30 days on land, air, sea 'to end the killings now.' Medinsky head Russian delegation 'satisfied with the outcome'; agreed 'each side will present its vision of a possible future cease-fire and spell it out in detail' for continued contacts. Ukraine handed Russia official list of children it says were forcibly deported and must be returned. Trump (per RFE/RL) called for direct Putin meeting following no-breakthrough talks. PRIOR MAY 13-14: ISTANBUL TRACK DOWNGRADED — PUTIN IN EFFECT REJECTED ZELENSKY CEASEFIRE OFFER. Russian President Vladimir Putin declined to attend Istanbul talks personally and instead appointed his aide Vladimir Medinsky to lead lower-level Russian delegation. President Zelensky en route to Ankara to meet Turkish President Erdogan May 13; will send Defense Minister Rustem Umerov-led delegation from Ankara to Istanbul to meet Russian delegation even though Moscow side 'doesn't include anyone who actually makes decisions.' Putin in effect rejected ceasefire offer and instead proposed restarting direct talks 'without preconditions.' Pokrovsk sector remains hottest: ~50 Russian attacks on Ukrainian positions May 12-13 in Pokrovsk + Kostiantynivka directions; clashes near Rodynske, Novooleksandrivka, Hryshyne, Bilytske, Pokrovsk, Kotlyne, Udachne, Muravka, Novopidhorodnie, Molodetske. Epicenter of fighting shifts toward RODYNSKE + KRASNYI LIMAN (north of Pokrovsk) along last corridor for Ukrainian forces defending Myrnohrad. Infantry activity on both sides decreased somewhat due to weather; Ukrainian Armed Forces still hold separate areas in Pokrovsk and Myrnohrad. Donetsk territorial sticking point unresolved (Moscow demanded Kyiv withdraw from areas Russia failed to capture; Ukraine refused). PRIOR MAY 12-13: PUTIN-ZELENSKY ISTANBUL DIPLOMATIC TRACK ACCELERATES. Russian President Vladimir Putin gathered Russian state TV in the middle of the night to inform them that he is ready to begin direct peace talks with Ukraine on May 15. President Volodymyr Zelensky said on May 13 he expects a ceasefire to result from a potential in-person meeting with Putin, which may take place in Istanbul on May 15: 'We will be waiting to meet with Putin in Turkey. So that Russia does not manipulate cities and say that Putin is not ready to fly to Ankara, but is ready to fly only to Istanbul.' Zelensky will meet with Turkish President Recep Tayyip Erdogan in Ankara before flying onward to Istanbul if Putin attends. Zelensky: 'We expect Russia to confirm a full, durable, and reliable ceasefire starting May 12, and Ukraine is ready to meet.' Kremlin spokesperson Dmitry Peskov on May 13 said the Kremlin would announce its representative once Putin 'deems it necessary.' Earlier the Russian president declined to attend personally and was poised to appoint aide Vladimir Medinsky to lead talks. PRIOR MAY 11-12: TRUMP-MEDIATED 3-DAY RUSSIA-UKRAINE CEASEFIRE EXPIRES TODAY MAY 11 — both sides accuse each other of breaches. Ukrainian authorities said Monday Russian drones, bombs and artillery struck civilian areas of northeastern Kharkiv and southern Kherson regions, killing at least 2 people and wounding 7 others, including a 14-year-old boy. CBC: 'A U.S.-brokered ceasefire between Russia and Ukraine was due to expire Monday with both sides accusing each other of breaching the 72-hour arrangement, as American and European officials considered how they might steer the warring countries into further talks.' PUTIN MAY 10-11: suggested Russia's war 'coming to an end'; willing to meet Zelensky in third country if peace deal finalized. DONETSK TERRITORIAL STICKING POINT: Moscow demanded Kyiv withdraw troops from parts of region Russian forces have failed to capture; Ukraine refused. POKROVSK MAY 11: 17 Russian assault attempts toward Bilytske, Nykanorivka, Dorozhnie, Rodynske, Novooleksandrivka, Udachne, Vasylivka, Molodetske, Novomykolaivka; 51 Russian attacks total on day of ceasefire expiry. 90TH TANK DIVISION still identified at Pokrovsk per Ukraine Air Assault Forces. PRIOR MAY 9-10: TRUMP-MEDIATED 3-DAY CEASEFIRE COLLAPSING IN PRACTICE. Zelensky said Russia had carried out MORE THAN 140 ATTACKS on frontline positions by early morning May 10, alongside 10 ASSAULTS + 850+ DRONE ATTACKS — dismissed ceasefire as ineffective. Kremlin said its forces downed 264 UKRAINIAN DRONES early Friday, with officials reporting attempted attacks on Moscow + the PERM REGION in the Ural Mountains (1,600+ km from front line). Defense News headline: 'Dueling Victory Day ceasefires for war in Ukraine collapse almost immediately.' POKROVSK MAY 9-10: 30+ Russian assaults repelled in Bilytske, Nykyforivka, Rodynske, Novooleksandrivka, Pokrovsk, Novopavlivka, Toretske, Nove Shakhove, Udachne, Molodetske, Hryshyne, Kotlyne; 200+ combat clashes total. Ukraine's Air Assault Forces reported the presence of Russia's 90th Tank Division at Pokrovsk. PRIOR MAY 9 VICTORY DAY: Moscow Red Square parade SCALED DOWN to infantry only — no tanks, no missiles, no armored vehicles for the first time in ~2 decades. Mobile internet cut for millions of users during parade. Foreign media accreditations revoked. Only confirmed foreign attendees: Belarus President Lukashenko, Laos President Thongloun Sisoulith, Malaysia Supreme Ruler Sultan Ibrahim Iskandar (shortest foreign-attendee list in modern Russian history). TRUMP ANNOUNCED 3-DAY RUSSIA-UKRAINE CEASEFIRE May 9-11 with 1,000-for-1,000 prisoner exchange; Kremlin and Zelensky confirmed; Zelensky pledged Ukraine will not attack Putin's Moscow parade in exchange for prisoner swap. POKROVSK MAY 8 PRIOR: 33 Russian assaults repelled; ~106,000 Russian personnel concentrated on Pokrovsk axis per Ukraine commander-in-chief; 208 total combat engagements in 24 hours; reported Russian losses +1,130. Ukrainian deep strikes May 7-8: 260+ drones intercepted across Russia, strikes reached PERM region in the Urals (1,600+ km from front line); May 8 Ukrainian drone hit air traffic control center, paralyzing southern Russian airports. PRIOR MAY 4: Ukrainian drone hit luxury Moscow high-rise ~7 km west of Red Square, ~3 km from MoD building. PRIOR MAY 7: Russia shot down 347 Ukrainian drones overnight in Ukraine's 2nd-largest aerial attack since the invasion — drones destroyed over 20 Russian regions including Moscow. Pokrovsk-direction Russian attempts to advance toward Nikanorivka, Rodinske, Novooleksandrivka, Shevchenko, Pokrovsk, Grishine, Sergiyivka, Molodetske; Russian forces reported 5,649 kamikaze drone uses + 1,862 settlement/position shellings. Russia unilateral MAY 8-9 Victory Day ceasefire begins today (May 8) with 'massive missile strike on Kyiv' threat backstop. Moscow parade scheduled May 9 takes place WITHOUT TANKS/MISSILES for first time in ~2 decades due to Ukrainian drone fears; mobile internet + text messaging to be shut down in Moscow May 9. Zelensky reported 1,820 Russian ceasefire violations by 10am May 6, including ~30 assault operations + 20+ airstrikes using 70+ glide bombs. PRIOR MAY 6: Russia +1,050 personnel to ~1,337,170 total combat losses since Feb 24, 2022 (Ukrainian General Staff). MAY 5 PRIOR: +970. RUSSIA BROKE UKRAINE'S UNILATERAL MAY 6 CEASEFIRE within MINUTES of its 12:00 a.m. start: launched 108 COMBAT DRONES + 3 missiles + 2 ballistic missiles + 1 Kh-31 air-to-surface missile overnight on May 6. 26 CIVILIANS KILLED + 118+ INJURED OVER PAST DAY across Ukraine. Russian targets: ENERGY FACILITIES, OIL/GAS INFRASTRUCTURE, RAILWAYS, INDUSTRIAL SITES, plus damage to homes, businesses, transportation network. Ukrainian FM Andrii Sybiha (May 6): 'Putin only cares about military parades, not human lives' — referring to Kremlin's own May 9 unilateral Victory Day truce. RUSSIA COUNTER-ACCUSED Kyiv of breaching its own ceasefire — Russian Foreign Ministry's Ambassador-at-Large Rodion Miroshnik said Ukraine launched attacks on Russian-occupied Crimea + Russia's Bryansk Oblast. POKROVSK SECTOR May 5: 34 enemy attacks recorded in Pokrovsk direction (155 combat clashes total May 5). Equipment losses past day per Ukrainian General Staff: tanks +1, armored combat vehicles +5, artillery +92, MLRS +5, air defense +2, UAVs +2,031, cruise missiles +1. Russian unilateral May 8-9 Victory Day truce still on books with 'massive missile strike on Kyiv' threat backstop. MAY 5 PRIOR: Russian strikes killed 22-26 across Ukraine — Kramatorsk 5 killed (3 aerial bombs), Zaporizhzhia 12 killed (4 guided bombs hit automobile repair shop ~4pm). Zelensky condemned Moscow's 'utter cynicism' for launching deadly attacks while seeking truce to stage May 9 parade. UKRAINIAN STRIKE killed 2 deep inside Russia overnight May 4-5; Moscow Victory Day parade pared down due to security concerns. Pentagon four-pressure-point posture (Iran ceasefire-with-MOU-track + Russia-Ukraine high-tempo + DPRK + Taiwan) sustained. 45 Russian attacks since start of day May 3, focusing main efforts on Pokrovsk + Kostiantynivka directions. Ukrainian defenders stopped 26 assault actions in morning toward Pokrovsk and other settlements; total 16 pushes during day. Ukraine's air defense destroyed/suppressed 175 Russian drones + 5 missiles between 08:30-18:30 May 3. Russian May 3 daytime attacks: dormitory in Dnipro damaged; 35 residential houses damaged in Chornomorsk suburbs (Odesa region). BELARUS BORDER FOLLOW-UP: Zelensky's May 2 'unusual activity' warning identified May 3 — Ukrainian State Border Guard confirmed entry of aerial target from Belarus side, identified as AIR BALLOON. Russia using Belarusian territory as LAUNCHPAD for SIGNAL-RELAY BALLOONS to extend drone connectivity into Ukrainian cities. February 2026 prior: Ukrainian hackers exposed 6-month operation showing Russia routing strike drones through Belarusian civilian cell towers + signal repeaters deployed on Belarusian territory H2 2025. Zelensky signed new SANCTIONS package May 3 including measures against Belarusian entities. Putin's May 9 Victory Day Ukraine ceasefire offer remains stalled — Zelensky publicly rejected parade-timed truce; Peskov May 1: 'no concrete decision'; Trump (Truth Social): 'I think he might do that.' Ukraine continues to demand LONG-TERM ceasefire. MAY 2 PRIOR: Russia +1,240 personnel; 51 combat engagements; Russia deployed ~1,600 attack drones + 1,100 guided bombs + 3 missiles past week; Ukrainian drone strike on civilian bus in Kherson killed 2 + injured 7. Donetsk Region Q1 2026 ratio: Russia losing 316 soldiers per 1 km² gained — DOUBLE the 160-per-km² figure same period 2025. Sawtooth tempo: Apr 27 (+810) → Apr 28 (+1,180) → Apr 29 (+1,180) → Apr 30 (+1,470) → May 1 (+1,420) → May 2 (+1,240) → May 3 (+1,080). Russia holds ~20%. Pokrovsk + Kostyantynivka axes hottest. Pentagon four-pressure-point posture persists (Iran blockade + Ukraine + DPRK + Taiwan). UKRAINE-GERMANY €4B defense deal (Apr 14).

theatres.summary: JUNE 19-20: Venezuela's removed president Nicolás Maduro and his wife Cilia Flores had their next New York court date postponed from June 30 to July 22, 2026; federal prosecutor Jay Clayton cited the need to avoid 'scheduling and logistical issues related to providing secure transportation and security measures' tied to the 2026 FIFA World Cup (the New York/New Jersey region hosting matches at MetLife Stadium, including the July 19 final). Delcy Rodríguez remains acting president of Venezuela; Cuba's fuel and grid crisis persists under the US blockade. (Cubaheadlines; PBS News; Wikipedia '2026 United States intervention in Venezuela,' June 2026.)  || [JUNE 15-16 UPDATE] Mid-June: situation broadly unchanged. Delcy Rodriguez remains acting president of Venezuela following the January US intervention and Maduro's capture; Maduro's US trial in New York continues. Cuba's oil/economic crisis persists under the American fuel blockade after the cutoff of Venezuelan oil. No major new June 15-16 developments. (CNN; PBS NewsHour; Wikipedia '2026 Cuban crisis,' June 2026.) [JUNE 5] CBS News reported CIA Director John Ratcliffe visited Havana for talks with senior Cuban officials, bringing a paramilitary leader involved in the Maduro-capture operation and introducing him as the operator who 'killed their people' in Venezuela. Maduro and Cilia Flores remain set to return to a Manhattan federal court June 30; Delcy Rodriguez continues as acting president in Caracas amid Cuba's persistent grid/fuel crisis. (CBS News; NBC News; ABC News, June 2026). [JUNE 1-2] Maduro and Cilia Flores remained set to return to a Manhattan federal court on June 30; Cuba's grid crisis persisted amid the loss of Venezuelan oil. (PBS; Fox Business, 2026). [MAY 31-JUNE 1] Maduro and Cilia Flores were set to return to a Manhattan federal court on June 30; Cuba's grid crisis persisted amid the loss of Venezuelan oil. MAY 15-16: CUBA grid collapse continues — Antonio Guiteras thermoelectric plant shut, SEN availability ~636 MW vs ~2,420 MW demand (74% unmet); Energy Minister: 'absolutely no fuel.' VENEZUELA: Maduro trial proceeds in NYC (judge weighing key issues, no ruling yet); Delcy Rodriguez acting president (US lifted her sanctions Apr 10); María Corina Machado weighing return; US-managed transition framing continues. || PRIOR: MAY 14 CUBA GRID COLLAPSE: Cuba experiencing one of its worst energy crises in decades following partial breakdown of National Electric System (SEN) on May 14. Failure began at 6:09 a.m. May 14, shortly after the country's largest power plant, ANTONIO GUITERAS thermoelectric plant, shut down at 4:58 a.m. due to a boiler leak. By 6:30 a.m. SEN's available capacity dwindled to mere 636 MW while demand reached 2,420 MW — leaving 1,790 MW of demand unmet (74% of total demand) — per Cuba Headlines + Al Jazeera + NPR + FMT + CiberCuba. Power outages in Havana stretched to 24 consecutive hours Thursday May 14; collapse stripped power from all eastern provinces from Guantánamo to Ciego de Ávila. Energy Min VICENTE DE LA O confirmed: 'We have absolutely no fuel (oil) and absolutely no diesel' (Jamaica Observer + FMT + CiberCuba). RUSSIAN UNIVERSAL TANKER (270K bbl diesel; left Vysotsk in January) still adrift in North Atlantic ~1,600km from Cuba; ETA pushed back to May 15 per Russian news + CubaHeadlines. CNN MAY 13: As US starves Cuba of oil, island pulling off one of fastest solar revolutions on the planet with China's help. UN declared humanitarian emergency April: 96K+ surgeries postponed, 1M+ relying on tanker trucks for water, 500K children facing reduced school hours. MAY 14 SOLAR DRIVE: Chinese-assisted solar buildout continuing under US blockade pressure. VENEZUELA: Rodriguez at The Hague (first out-of-Venezuela since Maduro abduction Jan 3) responded to Trump's May 11-12 'seriously considering' Venezuela 51st state Truth Social posts — said country 'would never surrender its independence': 'if there is one thing Venezuelan men and women have, it is that we love our independence process' (CNN, WSLS, RIO Times, Washington Post). Rodriguez was at ICJ on Guyana Essequibo dispute. PRIOR MAY 12-13 — TRUMP CUBA TALKS ANNOUNCEMENT: Trump on Truth Social Tuesday May 12 'Cuba is asking for help, and we are going to talk!!' — described communist-ruled island as 'a failed country.' Announcement made as Trump departed for China; no concrete details or negotiation agenda released; neither White House nor State Dept has explained how talks will unfold or US demands; no immediate Cuban government response. Marks surprise pivot from 'takeover' rhetoric (May 1 'almost immediately' Forum Club at Palm Beach) to talks-announcement track. Context: 240+ new sanctions since Jan 2026; at least 7 oil tankers intercepted; Cuba energy imports reduced 80-90%; blackouts affecting 55%+ of territory up to 25 hours daily; projected GDP contraction -7.2% for 2026. VENEZUELA ACTING PRES DELCY RODRIGUEZ at The Hague Monday May 11 (first time she's left Venezuela since Maduro abduction Jan 3) rejects Trump's 'serious consideration' of annexing Venezuela as 51st US state: 'is not foreseen and would never be foreseen.' Rodriguez reportedly compliant with US demands including stopping oil deliveries to Cuba, opening PDVSA to foreign firms, releasing political prisoners (Al Jazeera). Rodriguez heads to Hague for Guyana ICJ land dispute case. PRIOR MAY 3 — TRUMP MAY 1 EXECUTIVE ORDER EXPANDED CUBA SANCTIONS + 'TAKING OVER' RHETORIC: Trump signed executive order May 1 broadening US sanctions on Cuban government — targets persons, entities and affiliates supporting security apparatus; includes corruption + human rights violators; can apply to 'any foreign person' operating in 'energy, defense and related materiel, metals and mining, financial services, or security sector of the Cuban economy.' Speaking at Forum Club of the Palm Beaches in West Palm Beach Friday May 1, Trump said US would 'take over' Cuba 'almost immediately'; described scenario in which USS Abraham Lincoln (CVN-72) would be positioned ~100 yards off Cuban coast as it transits back from CENTCOM ('We'll bring it in, have it stop roughly 100 yards off the shore, and they'll say, thank you very much, we surrender'). Comments tied to ongoing US-Israeli war against Iran. President Diaz-Canel labeled Trump admin 'fascist'; 'no aggressor, no matter how powerful, will find surrender in Cuba'; asserted 'every Cuban is armed' against 'imminent US military threat.' CUBA MAY 2-3: power deficit ~1,500+ MW; Russian Universal tanker (251K bbl diesel; original ETA Apr 29) still moving erratically across North Atlantic, delayed at least until end of May per CiberCuba/CubaHeadlines; OFAC General License 134A speculated as cause of course deviation. Russian Anatoli Kolodkin tanker reserves (delivered Mar 30) rapidly depleting. Hermanos Diaz refinery (Santiago) still processing domestic heavy crude (forced substitution); Cuba's own oil production: ~40K bpd vs domestic demand 90-110K bpd. Health system backlog 96K+ pending surgeries (incl 11K children); ~1M people dependent on water trucking; worst since 1990s 'Special Period.' May Day 'La Patria Se Defiende' rallies May 1: 500K+ marchers per gov claim; Raul Castro + Diaz-Canel + Bruno Rodriguez at José Martí Anti-Imperialist Tribune opposite US Embassy. PETRO-RODRIGUEZ Apr 24 Caracas visit (first head-of-state since Maduro abduction Jan 3) holds; military cooperation pledge on 2,200km border. RODRIGUEZ exceeded constitutional 90-day acting-presidency cap (Apr 21). MADURO PLEADED NOT GUILTY (Apr 13); next hearing Mar 17, 2027. US Embassy resuming operations. 100+ demonstrations in March (highest since ACLED 2018). GDP -7.2% forecast. Colombia: FARC dissident clashes intensified; EMC attacks drove 35% increase in violence in Cauca; Colombia internal security raised at UNSC Apr 21.

theatres.summary: [JUNE 15-16 UPDATE] Mid-June: relations in a 'stabilization' phase after the Trump-Xi trade truce, but Taiwan friction persists — in early June Taiwan's coast guard expelled four Chinese government ships that entered restricted waters off the island's southern tip, with both sides trading warnings. Xi has signaled willingness to make 2026 a 'landmark year' for US-China relations while warning Taiwan is the 'most important' issue. No military escalation in the Iran-war window. (CNBC; SCMP; ChinaPower/CSIS, May-June 2026.) [JUNE 1-2] The one-year trade truce reached at the May 14-15 Beijing Trump-Xi summit (which paused China's extreme rare-earth export-licensing regime) continued to hold, expiring around November 2026 with no clear signs yet of an extension; Taiwan remained the central flashpoint after Xi's warning that mishandling it could put 'the entire relationship in great jeopardy.' (CFR; CNBC, May 2026). [MAY 30-31] At the Shangri-La Dialogue in Singapore, Secretary of War Hegseth said the US seeks a 'stable equilibrium' with China in the Indo-Pacific, praised Philippines/Australia/Indonesia/Malaysia/Singapore for 'burden-sharing,' urged Vietnam and India to improve readiness, and warned Beijing not to disrupt the status quo; Chinese DM Dong Jun skipped the forum a second year. It was the first US Indo-Pacific policy signal since the May 14 Trump-Xi Beijing summit, where the two sides agreed to reset ties and manage disputes. MAY 15-16: Trump-Xi Beijing summit CONCLUDED with divergent readouts. metrics.value: JULY 8 — Traffic stayed cautious as US 'additional strikes' hit 60+ IRGC small boats used to harass shipping and Trump threatened to blockade Iran again; the Strait stayed physically open (blockade lifted, Day 21) but shipowners re-priced war risk after the July 7 tanker attacks. No US reimposition of the blockade was ordered. (Al Jazeera; CNBC, July 8, 2026.) || JULY 7 — Traffic disrupted anew as Iran attacked three tankers off Oman's coast; at least eight Japan-linked vessels (including five VLCCs) exited Hormuz via a route near Iran, and shipowners turned cautious again. Overall flows had been running above 10M bpd on an uneven recovery; the attacks reintroduced diversion and slowdown risk on the southern/Omani route. Still well below the pre-war ~130 vessels/day. (CNBC; Al Jazeera, July 7, 2026.) || JULY 6-7 — Traffic held an uneven recovery with total Hormuz flows above 10M bpd; ~40 vessels/day returning as conditions stabilize (northern/Iranian and southern/Omani routes open; central channel still clearing mines). Still below the pre-war ~130/day. (CNBC; Travel And Tour World, July 2026.) || JULY 5-6 — Total Strait of Hormuz crude/condensate flows recovered above 10M bpd (Saudi exports ~90% of pre-war, UAE >3.9M bpd), though tanker traffic stayed below the pre-crisis ~84/day baseline and many vessels ran with AIS off. Reopening is proceeding by negotiation; Iran reaffirmed mid-August transit 'service fees' (US rejects) and warned against 'extra-regional' naval movements, while the UK/France backed an Oman-led free-navigation effort. (CNBC/EIA; Wikipedia/PortWatch, July 1-5, 2026.) || JULY 4-5 — Recovery stayed gradual and uneven through the funeral-week pause; no new incidents. PortWatch/monitoring showed 43 transits July 1 (24 inbound, 19 outbound) against a pre-crisis baseline of ~84/day, with many vessels running with AIS off (so real counts likely higher). Iran's deputy FM issued a 'serious warning' to France and the UK over their naval movements in the Strait and reiterated 'service fees' from mid-August, while the UK and France pledged to work with Oman on 'safe transit for ships of all nations.' Still far below pre-war norms; reopening by negotiation, not a US seizure. (Wikipedia '2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis'/PortWatch; CBS News, July 1-4, 2026.) || JULY 2-3 — Traffic kept recovering as the Doha round and the ceasefire held: 258 vessels transited the Strait in the prior week, up from 138 the week before, though still far below the pre-war ~130/day; major container lines resumed Gulf services. Iran's joint military command warned all tankers to use its Tehran-designated routes or face a 'forceful response,' and state media reported a foreign container ship ran aground outside the designated corridor. (CBS News; Gulf News; The Bridge Chronicle, July 2-3, 2026.) || JUNE 29-30 — Traffic stayed thinned by the weekend clashes but recovery resumed. After the June 27-28 strikes, 29 commodity vessels crossed Hormuz on Saturday and 12 on Sunday, down from ~70 the prior Wednesday; following the June 29 US-Iran stand-down major container lines resumed Gulf services and the first commercial flight from Tehran landed in Dubai, with Persian Gulf exports near ~75% of pre-war (~4.8M bpd, still below the ~15M bpd pre-war). Hundreds of vessels remain stranded inside the Gulf and shipowners stay cautious pending demining. (CBS News; Euronews; The National; TradingEconomics, June 29, 2026.) || JUNE 28-29 — Hormuz stayed open through the broadened exchange. Oil flows remained near ~4.8 million bpd since the US-Iran deal (the highest since the war began Feb 28, still below the ~15M bpd pre-war), with Gulf exports near ~75% of pre-war and the US-Navy JMIC's widened transit route near Oman in effect. Iran reasserted that the Strait is under its 'total oversight and management' (Araghchi) but did not re-close it; the US kept it open. (Al Jazeera; RFE/RL, June 28, 2026.) || JUNE 27-28 — Hormuz kept reopening even through the two-day kinetic exchange. Oil flows rose to ~4.8 million bpd since the US-Iran deal — the highest since the war began on Feb 28, though still well below the ~15 million bpd of pre-war transits — with Gulf exports back to roughly 75% of pre-war levels. The US-Navy Joint Maritime Information Center (JMIC) announced a WIDENED route through the Strait near Oman on June 27, allowing increased naval traffic in both directions; Trump confirmed the Strait remains open and traffic continues. (CNBC; 2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis timeline; RFE/RL, June 24-27, 2026.) || JUNE 26-27 — Traffic held a war-period high even through the kinetic exchange: 70 vessels transited the Strait on June 25 (the most in a single day since March 1) versus ~35 the prior day, via the open northern (Iranian) and southern (Omani) routes; the UN IMO's shepherding/evacuation program stayed paused after the June 25 Ever Lovely drone strike, and on June 26 the IRGC turned back three foreign tankers that crossed 'without coordinating with Iranian authorities.' The US naval blockade remains lifted; the central channel stays closed pending ~80 mines. Still under a quarter of the pre-war ~120-130/day. (Al Jazeera Economy; Fox News, June 26, 2026.) || JUNE 25-26 — Traffic continued but the UN International Maritime Organization PAUSED its program to shepherd/evacuate ships through the Strait after Iran struck a cargo vessel near Oman on June 25; the IRGC Navy warned safe passage would be permitted only via Tehran-designated routes. Recovery had reached ~30 crossings/day (>20 tankers / ~35M barrels since the reopening) — still under a quarter of the pre-war ~120-130/day; the central channel stays closed pending ~80 mines. (NBC News; CBC News, June 25, 2026.) || JUNE 24-25 — Traffic held its war-period high: 109 vessels transited Saturday-Monday and ~25 ships crossed the prior Thursday (13 west-to-east, 12 east-to-west), still a fraction of the pre-war ~120-130/day. Open via the northern (Iranian) and southern (Omani) routes; the central channel stays closed pending ~80 mines. Tehran allowing toll-free transit for the 60-day window; Iran's Persian Gulf Strait Authority said planned fees are suspended during that window. (Fox Business; CNBC; Al Jazeera, June 22-24, 2026.) || JUNE 23-24 — Traffic rose to its highest since the conflict began at end-February: 109 vessels transited the Strait of Hormuz from Saturday through Monday, still below the pre-war ~120-130/day, with a backlog of hundreds awaiting passage and the central channel still being de-mined. Iran asserted that transits now require its authorization and signaled possible transit charges via a compulsory-insurance framework, even as the US naval blockade remained lifted. (AOL/Fox Business; CNBC; Times of Israel, June 22-23, 2026.) || JUNE 22-23 — The June 20 closure dispute was diplomatically defused: at the Bürgenstock talks (June 22) Iran and the US agreed to set up communication lines to keep the Strait of Hormuz open, meant to ensure it stays 'fully open.' Traffic remained well below the pre-war ~120-130 transits/day and reopening is still gradual (central channel mined; ~500+ vessels were waiting to exit the Gulf), but the status moved from a hard Iranian closure declaration toward a managed, communications-channel reopening — a negotiated mechanism, not a US ground seizure. (CBS News; CNBC, June 22, 2026.) || JUNE 20-22 — Traffic remained well below the pre-war ~120-130 transits/day. The US (CENTCOM) reported 55 merchant ships carrying >17 million barrels transited the strait on June 20 despite Iran's closure declaration ('traffic continues to flow'), with an estimated 500+ vessels still waiting to exit the Gulf; the closure-vs-flow status is disputed between Iran and the US. (CNN live; CBS News live blog, June 20-21, 2026.) || JUNE 20-21 — IRAN RE-CLOSED THE STRAIT FROM ITS OWN SIDE. After four days of a tentative reopening, Iran's IRGC declared the Strait of Hormuz closed again on June 20 in protest at Israel's continued Lebanon strikes, which Tehran casts as a US failure to enforce the MOU; Iran warned of 'reciprocal action.' The US naval blockade itself remains LIFTED (CENTCOM enforcement 'ceased') — the new closure is an Iranian coercive measure, not a return of US interdiction. Traffic, already a trickle (Lloyd's List had ~550 ships still to exit the Gulf; central route closed pending ~80 mines), is again disrupted; ~80M barrels of crude were reported lined up to exit. Talks to resolve it were due to reconvene Sunday June 21 (Vance to Bürgenstock). Negotiated/coerced reopening contest, not a ground seizure. (Al Jazeera, 'Iran closes Strait of Hormuz as Pakistan says new talks with US due Sunday'; oilprice.com, June 20, 2026.) || JUNE 19-20 — REOPENING CONTINUES, STILL A TRICKLE. CENTCOM said 'American forces are not impeding the transit of vessels to or from Iranian ports' and that 'all U.S. military blockade enforcement efforts have ceased'; sanctioned Iranian tankers entered the strait and Grimaldi Group, Cosco and Knutsen vessels were among those transiting (at least 10 Thursday morning per CBS). But Lloyd's List estimated ~550 merchant ships still need to exit the Gulf, the central channel stays closed pending clearance of ~80 mines, and full normalization is 'weeks' away. Negotiated reopening, not a ground seizure. (CBS News; CNBC; Lloyd's List, June 18-19, 2026.) || JUNE 18 — REOPENING BEGAN. With the MOU signed (June 17) and the US blockade lifted, commercial traffic returned to the Strait of Hormuz for the first time in ~110 days: Windward counted ~18 vessels transiting between 6 p.m. June 17 and 2 p.m. UTC June 18 (a French-flagged LNG tanker, two Hong Kong-flagged tankers, an Italian-flagged vehicle carrier, a Japanese-controlled oil tanker, Saudi-flagged tankers); CBS reported at least 10 transits Thursday morning. Ships are using the northern (Iranian) and southern (Omani) routes while the central channel stays closed pending clearance of ~80 mines; analyst Michelle Wiese Bockmann called it 'a sign of confidence' that will 'start as a trickle,' and CNBC said full normalization will take weeks. VP Vance said '12.5 million barrels of oil passed through... last night' (a war-era high) but warned 'no tolls or no deal,' against Iran's signal it will 'charge fees for services' jointly with Oman. Still far below the ~135 ships/day pre-war norm; negotiated reopening, not a ground seizure. (Windward via CBS/CNBC; Lloyd's List; Al Jazeera, June 17-18, 2026.) || JUNE 17 — Strait still CLOSED in practice despite the ceasefire. ADNOC CEO Sultan Al Jaber said Hormuz is not open because Iran is restricting and conditioning traffic, with ~230 loaded oil tankers waiting inside the Gulf; third-country transit is expected to resume only once the deal takes effect (Friday June 19 signing). Traffic remains far below the ~120-140 ships/day pre-war baseline. (Wikipedia '2026 Strait of Hormuz crisis'; industry reporting, June 2026.) || JUNE 16-17 — Hormuz remains effectively closed; current traffic is ~12-15 ships/day against a pre-war average of 120-140. Reopening begins only after Friday's signing, starting with mine removal by an international naval mission (US, UK, France, Germany) using drone boats and minesweepers; insurers/shippers estimate 40-50 days before transiting in volume, against the MOU's 'within 30 days' removal target. Negotiated-reopening pathway, not a ground seizure. (Jerusalem Post; Globe and Mail; Marine Insight; Claims Journal, June 16, 2026.) || JUNE 15-16 — Hormuz remains effectively closed to commercial traffic pending Friday's signing; under the finalized MOU it reopens for mine removal after the deal is signed, with Iran clearing its own mines. Analysts cautioned normalization will be gradual — war-risk insurer Svein Ringbakken said restoration to normal 'would take months' even at full capacity, and shipping executive S.V. Anchan predicted 'over a year.' Trump had authorized the toll-free reopening; the US energy secretary said Hormuz ship traffic was increasing. (Al Jazeera; NBC News, June 15, 2026.) || JUNE 14-15 — Trump authorized the toll-free reopening of the Strait of Hormuz and the immediate removal of the US naval blockade as part of the June 14 deal; Defense Secretary Hegseth said the reopening would begin 'immediately' but contingent on Iranian performance, targeting pre-war volumes within ~30 days, with Iran responsible for clearing its own mines (potentially into mid-2027). Actual transits remained minimal as of this update and some tankers reportedly paused amid Israel's June 14 Lebanon strikes; the reopening is authorized but not yet realized pending the Friday signing. (PBS NewsHour; CBS News; Axios, June 14, 2026.) || JUNE 13-14 — The Strait of Hormuz remains effectively CLOSED pending a signing, but the trajectory points to reopening: Trump said the deal would be signed Sunday June 14 and that 'immediately after it is signed, the Hormuz Strait is OPEN TO ALL,' and the US energy secretary said Strait ship traffic was increasing (some flow moving with transponders off / Navy coordination). Traffic still near-zero (~36/week vs ~130/day pre-war) as of this update. (Bloomberg; CNBC, June 9-13, 2026.) || JUNE 12-13 — The Strait of Hormuz remains effectively CLOSED (IRGC 'closed to all ships,' June 10), with traffic near-zero (~36/week vs ~130/day pre-war) and the conflict still kinetic at sea: overnight June 11-12 Iranian drones fired on Indian commercial shipping leaving the strait and US forces downed two Iranian drones (Trump: 'totally unacceptable'). JULY 9 (Day 133): Status holds no_ground_troops at the war's sharpest rhetorical peak since the MOU. On July 8 Trump, from the NATO Ankara summit, declared the ceasefire and the Islamabad MOU 'over' ('a waste of time'; Iran 'vicious, violent'; 'every time they hit us, we hit them 20') and threatened to bomb and blockade Iran again, and US CENTCOM ran its largest post-MOU strike wave — 'additional strikes' aggregating to 80+ targets and 60+ IRGC small boats plus air-defense, C2, coastal-radar, surveillance and anti-ship-missile sites, with explosions at two locations in southern Iran. Yet the execution stayed air and maritime: every US ground-execution indicator remained at zero — no US troops in Iran, no Kharg assault, no new ARG/MEU order, no draft; blockade still lifted (Day 21) — and the president walked the 'over' remark back the same day ('I don't think it's going to start again'). Standing posture (Stars and Stripes, July 1): ~50,000 troops, ~24 warships (carriers Abraham Lincoln and George H.W. Bush, 15 destroyers), with USS Boxer ARG / 11th MEU and USS Tripoli ARG / 31st MEU in the Arabian Sea in routine/contingency posture. Brent's move to $78/bbl is war-risk repricing, far below ground-commitment pricing. Separately, Khamenei was buried at Mashhad's Imam Reza shrine July 9, closing the state funeral; new Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei still had not appeared publicly. daily_entries.headline: DAY 133 — CEASEFIRE DECLARED 'OVER' BY TRUMP, THEN WALKED BACK THE SAME DAY / US BLOCKADE LIFTED DAY 21 — KINETIC CYCLE INTENSIFIED BUT STAYED AIR/MARITIME. daily_entries.summary: The breach-retaliation cycle that reopened July 7 intensified on July 8 without changing rungs. US CENTCOM said it had begun 'additional strikes against Iran to further degrade their ability to threaten freedom of navigation in the Strait of Hormuz' — a second retaliatory wave layered on the July 7 package. Aggregating the reporting, the campaign hit 80+ targets, including more than 60 IRGC small boats used to harass shipping, plus air defenses, command-and-control, coastal-radar and surveillance sites, anti-ship-missile capabilities, and underground drone/missile storage; explosions and activated air defenses were reported at two locations in southern Iran. From the NATO summit in Ankara, President Trump declared the ceasefire and the Islamabad MOU 'over' — calling the agreement 'a waste of time,' Iran 'vicious, violent,' and warning 'every time they hit us, we hit them 20' with a threat to bomb and blockade Iran again — the sharpest US escalation rhetoric since the MOU. Hours later he walked it back, saying 'I don't think it's going to start again' and that the exchange would not lead to long-term military action; oil eased off its highs on the reversal, with Brent settling +5.2% at $78.02/bbl and WTI up in step. Despite the peak rhetoric, every US ground-execution indicator stayed at zero: no US troops entered Iran, no Kharg assault or port seizure was ordered or executed, no new amphibious/Marine landing order issued, and no draft or mobilization signal appeared. The US answer to Iranian maritime coercion remained an air/stand-off strike package plus the July 7 oil-waiver revocation — the structural inverse of a Kharg landing — and the naval blockade stayed lifted (Day 21). Separately, the six-day state funeral for slain Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei closed on July 9 with burial at the Imam Reza shrine in Mashhad, his birthplace and Iran's holiest city, after rites in Tehran, Qom, Najaf and Karbala. New Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, designated in early March, still had not appeared publicly, keeping the who-governs-Iran question live.

daily_entries.summary: After five straight days off the kinetic register, the Iran war's breach-retaliation cycle resumed on July 7 during the funeral week. Iran's Revolutionary Guard attacked three commercial vessels near the Strait of Hormuz off Oman's coast: the Qatar-flagged LNG carrier Al-Rekayyat (struck by a projectile ~8 miles east of Limah, sparking an engine-room fire), the Saudi-flagged crude supertanker Wedyan (damaged by an Iranian-fired missile), and a third tanker hit by a drone (minor structural damage per UKMTO); no casualties were reported. Iranian state TV said the ships had ignored warnings about Tehran-approved transit routes. US Central Command responded with what it called 'a series of powerful strikes against Iran' — described as larger than prior retaliatory packages — hitting air defenses, coastal-surveillance and radar sites, surface-to-air and anti-ship cruise-missile batteries, drone-launch sites and port facilities, with explosions reported near Bandar Abbas, Qeshm Island, Bandar Khamir and the port of Sirik along Iran's southern coast. The Treasury's OFAC revoked the general license that had allowed Iranian oil and petrochemical sales, effective immediately with a wind-down by July 17. Iran's Foreign Ministry called the strikes and revocation a 'blatant violation' of the mid-June Islamabad MOU, vowed 'decisive actions to preserve its security,' and warned that final-deal negotiations 'will not commence if threats continue'; US-Iran talks were already paused for the funeral week. Oil, which had slid to a four-month low near the pre-war ~$72/bbl, spiked: Brent rose ~5.5% to about $76/bbl (settling ~$74.16, +3%) and WTI ~5% to about $72. The escalation stayed on the air/missile and maritime rungs — the US answer to Iranian maritime coercion was an air-strike package, not a Kharg landing or port seizure, and every US ground-execution indicator remained at zero: no US troops in Iran, no Kharg assault, no new ARG/MEU order, no draft; the naval blockade stayed lifted (Day 20). In parallel, the state funeral for slain Supreme Leader Ayatollah Ali Khamenei moved into Iraq on July 8 — an official reception at Najaf International Airport, a procession toward the Shrine of Imam Ali, and rites at the Imam Hussein shrine in Karbala, with President Pezeshkian, Speaker Ghalibaf and Khamenei's eldest son attending — ahead of final burial at the Imam Reza shrine in Mashhad, Khamenei's birthplace, on July 9. New Supreme Leader Mojtaba Khamenei, named March 9, still had not appeared publicly.

IRAN VOWS 'DECISIVE ACTIONS'; TALKS AT RISK (July 7-8, 2026): Iran's Foreign Ministry accused the US of violating the MOU and said Iran will take 'decisive actions to preserve its security'; the FM warned that negotiations on a final deal 'will not commence if threats continue.' Indirect US-Iran talks remained paused for the funeral week (to resume after the July 9 burial per Qatar). No Iranian retaliatory strike had been confirmed by the morning of July 8. (Washington Times; Times of Israel; Al Jazeera, July 7-8, 2026.)

OIL SPIKES OFF THE FOUR-MONTH LOW (July 7, 2026): Brent rose ~5.5% to about $76/bbl (September) and settled ~$74.16 (+3%); WTI advanced ~5% to about $72 (August). The move reversed the post-ceasefire slide that had taken Brent to a four-month low near the pre-war ~$72/bbl, but stayed far below the $110+ wartime peaks and the $130+ a US ground commitment would imply. (CNBC; CBS News, July 7, 2026.)

FUNERAL MOVES TO IRAQ, THEN MASHHAD (July 8-9, 2026): Khamenei's cortege crossed into Iraq for a reception at Najaf International Airport and processions at the Shrine of Imam Ali (Najaf) and Imam Hussein shrine (Karbala) on July 8, with President Pezeshkian, Speaker Ghalibaf and Khamenei's eldest son attending, ahead of burial at the Imam Reza shrine in Mashhad on July 9. daily_entries.prediction_impact: July 7-8 is analytically important but does NOT rehabilitate Predictive History's imminent-US-ground-invasion / Hormuz-and-Kharg-seizure thesis — it reinforces the disconfirmed-and-inverted pattern. The five-day off-the-kinetic streak broke, but into the same breach-retaliation cycle seen in late June: Iran does the maritime attacking (three tankers) and the US answers with an AIR strike package plus an economic move (oil-waiver revocation), not a Kharg landing or port seizure. Every US ground-execution indicator stayed at zero and the blockade stayed lifted (Day 20), so the ground rung is unchanged. The structural inversion holds and even sharpens: it is Iran, not the US, using force to assert control over Hormuz transit ('designated routes'), the opposite of the predicted US seizure. The escalation does bear on two live open questions — deal durability (iran-us-deal-reached-june-2026), now under direct kinetic strain with Iran threatening to withhold final-deal talks, and Hormuz governance (iran-hormuz-administration-tolls-dispute-june-2026), now being contested by force rather than only by toll claims — and it re-instances the breach-vs-return-to-war ambiguity tracked in june3-kuwait-kinetic-escalation-2026. The oil spike to ~$76/bbl is a war-risk repricing, still far below ground-commitment pricing.

alternate_readings.reading: The July 7 tanker attacks and US 'powerful strikes' admit the same two readings that have run through every prior breach-retaliation round. One treats the exchange as coercive bargaining inside a still-live, war-ended MOU: Iran signalling over Hormuz transit rules and the US imposing 'heavy costs' to deter, both stopping at the air/maritime rung with no casualties and no ground move, and with talks only paused rather than cancelled. The other treats it as the leading edge of a return to open war — a ceasefire now materially breached, Iran vowing 'decisive actions' and threatening to withhold final-deal talks, the US revoking the oil waiver and striking harder than before — that could spiral back to sustained hostilities.
alternate_readings.evidentiary_status: Both readings rest on the same on-record facts: Iran attacked three tankers off Oman on July 7; CENTCOM struck air-defense, coastal, missile, drone and port sites near Bandar Abbas/Qeshm/Sirik; OFAC revoked the GL X oil waiver (wind-down July 17); Iran's FM called it an MOU violation and vowed 'decisive actions'; no casualties and no ground movement were reported; talks stayed paused for the funeral, not cancelled. Which reading is correct depends on whether Iran executes a materially escalatory retaliation and whether the post-funeral round convenes — neither determinable from open sources on July 8.
public_assertion_by: US CENTCOM / Treasury (July 7, 2026): the strikes and oil-waiver revocation are calibrated 'heavy costs' to deter attacks on shipping, not a war restart.
Iran Foreign Ministry (Gharibabadi, July 7, 2026): the US committed a 'blatant violation' of the MOU; Iran will take 'decisive actions' and will not open final-deal talks 'if threats continue.'
Analysts / maritime-security reporting: frame the tanker strikes as Iran enforcing 'designated routes,' consistent with coercive Hormuz bargaining rather than general war.
Some commentators: read the largest-yet US strike package plus a materially breached ceasefire as evidence the interim peace is unravelling.
alternate_readings.why_unresolvable: Resolution requires knowing whether Iran mounts a materially escalatory retaliation (beyond the tanker attacks) and whether the post-funeral negotiation actually reconvenes; as of July 8 open sources show only the July 7 exchange, an oil-waiver revocation, and Iranian threats, consistent with both a contained coercive round and the start of a slide back to war.

daily_entries.headline: DAY 132 GROUND-INVASION TRACKER — STATUS HOLDS no_ground_troops DESPITE THE KINETIC CYCLE RESUMING. THE FIVE-DAY OFF-THE-KINETIC STREAK BROKE ON JULY 7 (IRAN ATTACKED THREE TANKERS NEAR HORMUZ; US CENTCOM ANSWERED WITH ITS LARGEST 'POWERFUL STRIKES' PACKAGE AND OFAC REVOKED IRAN'S OIL WAIVER), BUT THE EXCHANGE STAYED ON THE AIR/MISSILE AND MARITIME RUNGS. EVERY US GROUND-EXECUTION INDICATOR REMAINED AT ZERO: NO US TROOPS IN IRAN, NO KHARG ASSAULT, NO NEW ARG/MEU ORDER, NO DRAFT; BLOCKADE STILL LIFTED (DAY 20). THE US RESPONSE TO IRANIAN MARITIME COERCION WAS AN AIR-STRIKE PACKAGE ON AIR-DEFENSE, COASTAL, MISSILE, DRONE AND PORT SITES NEAR BANDAR ABBAS/QESHM/SIRIK — THE STRUCTURAL INVERSE OF A KHARG LANDING. NO NEW TROOP MOVEMENTS, GROUND-OPERATION AUTHORIZATIONS, PENTAGON GROUND STATEMENTS OR DRAFT SIGNALS ACCOMPANIED THE STRIKES. STANDING IN-THEATRE POSTURE UNCHANGED (STARS AND STRIPES, JULY 1): ~50,000 US TROOPS AND ~24 WARSHIPS (CARRIERS ABRAHAM LINCOLN AND GEORGE H.W. BUSH, 15 DESTROYERS), WITH USS BOXER ARG / 11TH MEU (IN-THEATRE SINCE JUNE 30) AND USS TRIPOLI ARG / 31ST MEU IN THE ARABIAN SEA IN ROUTINE/CONTINGENCY POSTURE — NO LANDING ORDERED OR EXECUTED. IT IS IRAN, NOT THE US, USING FORCE TO ASSERT CONTROL OVER HORMUZ TRANSIT — THE INVERSE OF THE PREDICTED US SEIZURE. BRENT'S SPIKE TO ~$76/BBL IS WAR-RISK REPRICING, STILL FAR BELOW GROUND-COMMITMENT PRICING.
daily_entries.summary: The ground-invasion track held at no_ground_troops even as the war's kinetic register reopened on July 7. Iran's IRGC attacked three tankers near the Strait of Hormuz, US CENTCOM launched what it called its largest retaliatory strike package to date, and the Treasury revoked Iran's oil-sales waiver — but the entire exchange stayed on the air/missile and maritime rungs. No US ground troops entered Iran, no Kharg assault was ordered or executed, no new amphibious/Marine landing order was issued, and no draft or mobilization signal appeared. The US answer to Iranian maritime coercion was an air-strike package against air-defense, coastal-surveillance, SAM, anti-ship cruise-missile, drone-launch and port targets near Bandar Abbas, Qeshm Island, Bandar Khamir and Sirik — the structural inverse of a landing to seize Iran's oil-export hub. The standing footprint was unchanged from the spring buildup: ~50,000 troops, two carriers, 15 destroyers, and two amphibious ready groups (Boxer/11th MEU and Tripoli/31st MEU) in the Arabian Sea in routine/contingency posture; reported 82nd Airborne elements in-region remain part of that standing posture, not a new July order. The blockade stayed lifted (Day 20). The predicted US Hormuz/Kharg seizure stays disconfirmed-and-inverted: it is Iran using force to assert transit control, and Brent's spike to ~$76/bbl is war-risk repricing well below the $130+ a ground commitment would imply.
details: NO GROUND EXECUTION DESPITE ESCALATION (July 7-8): The resumed breach-retaliation cycle produced no US troops in Iran, no Kharg assault, no new ARG/MEU landing order, and no draft. Bush, 15 destroyers); USS Boxer ARG / 11th MEU (in-theatre since June 30) and USS Tripoli ARG / 31st MEU in the Arabian Sea in routine/contingency posture; reported 82nd Airborne elements are part of the standing spring buildup, not a new July order.

INVERSION SHARPENS: Iran, not the US, used force to assert control over Hormuz transit ('designated routes'), and the US answered from the air and with an oil-waiver revocation — the opposite of the predicted US seizure of Kharg/Iranian oil. (Al Jazeera; CBS News, July 7, 2026.)

daily_entries.headline: RUSSIA-UKRAINE — NATO ANKARA SUMMIT (JULY 7-8) CONFIRMS €70BN ($80BN) 2026 UKRAINE AID; TRUMP-ZELENSKY MEET; AIR DEFENSE THE CENTRAL ASK: NATO'S 32 LEADERS PLUS ZELENSKY AND SOUTH KOREA'S LEE JAE-MYUNG MET IN ANKARA. ALLIES CONFIRMED A COMMITMENT TO PROVIDE €70 BILLION ($80B) IN MILITARY EQUIPMENT, AID AND TRAINING FOR UKRAINE IN 2026 (LARGELY A REPACKAGING OF EXISTING NATO/EU FUNDING RATHER THAN NEW MONEY) AND SET A GOAL OF AT LEAST AN EQUIVALENT LEVEL IN 2027. ZELENSKY USED HIS TRUMP BILATERAL TO PRESS FOR PATRIOT SYSTEMS AND INTERCEPTOR MISSILES AFTER THE JULY 6 RUSSIAN BARRAGE ON THE KYIV REGION KILLED ~22 (15 IN KYIV CITY) AND INJURED ~90, WHICH UKRAINE COULD NOT INTERCEPT FOR LACK OF INTERCEPTORS. KOSTIANTYNIVKA STAYED CONTESTED — RUSSIA'S JULY 3 'LIBERATION' CLAIM REMAINED DISPUTED, WITH ISW ASSESSING SMALL-GROUP INFILTRATION, NOT CONSOLIDATED CONTROL. NO US GROUND-DEPLOYMENT SURGE.
daily_entries.summary: The NATO summit in Ankara (July 7-8) closed with allies confirming a commitment to €70 billion ($80B) in military equipment, aid and training for Ukraine in 2026 and a goal of maintaining at least an equivalent level in 2027 — though analysts noted the €70B figure largely repackages existing NATO annual commitments and EU-loan funding rather than adding new money. President Trump and President Zelensky held a bilateral in which Zelensky pressed for additional Patriot air-defense systems and, above all, interceptor missiles, citing the July 6 Russian barrage on the Kyiv region that killed roughly 22 people (15 in the capital) and injured about 90, and which Ukraine could not shoot down for lack of interceptors. NATO Secretary General Rutte framed the summit around three priorities — higher allied defense spending, stronger transatlantic defense-industrial production (including possible European coproduction of Patriot interceptors), and continued support for Ukraine. On the ground, Kostiantynivka remained contested: Russia's July 3 claim to have 'liberated' the city stayed disputed by Kyiv, with ISW continuing to assess small-group infiltration rather than consolidated control. There was no US ground-deployment surge and no change to the war's territorial baseline (Russia holds ~20% of Ukraine).
details: NATO ANKARA SUMMIT OUTCOME (July 7-8, 2026): 32 NATO leaders plus non-member guests Zelensky and South Korea's President Lee Jae-myung attended. TRUMP-ZELENSKY BILATERAL / AIR DEFENSE (July 7-8, 2026): Zelensky pressed Trump for more Patriot systems and interceptor missiles, warning of an 'insufficient supply of interceptors'; a realistic outcome floated was US backfilling of European air-defense gaps and possible European coproduction of Patriot interceptors. Germany is financing two Patriot systems. (Time; Newsweek; Foreign Policy, July 6-8, 2026.)

JULY 6 KYIV BARRAGE (context): Russia's overnight ballistic-and-drone barrage on the Kyiv region killed ~22 nationwide (15 in Kyiv city, 8 in the wider region) and injured ~90; Ukraine could not intercept the ballistic missiles for lack of interceptors, sharpening Zelensky's summit ask. (CNN; Time; Inquirer, July 5-6, 2026.)

KOSTIANTYNIVKA STILL CONTESTED (July 6-8, 2026): Russia's July 3 'liberation' claim (Gerasimov to Putin) stayed disputed; Zelensky called it 'a lie' and ISW/DeepState continued to assess small-group infiltration, not consolidated control. Russia holds ~20% of Ukraine with no confirmed net change. (ISW; Kyiv Independent, July 6-8, 2026.)

daily_entries.headline: LATIN AMERICA — CUBA NATIONWIDE BLACKOUT (JULY 6) DEEPENS AS US OIL BLOCKADE DRAGS ON; VENEZUELA MANDATE DISPUTE, MADURO TRIAL JULY 22: CUBA'S ENTIRE NATIONAL GRID COLLAPSED AT MIDDAY JULY 6 — THE THIRD/FOURTH TOTAL BLACKOUT OF 2026 — LEAVING ~10 MILLION WITHOUT POWER; GRID OPERATOR UNE SERVED ~1% OF HAVANA'S DEMAND BY LATE AFTERNOON, WITH RESTORATION UNDERWAY JULY 7-8. THE COLLAPSE IS DRIVEN BY A DE FACTO US OIL BLOCKADE, A CRUMBLING GRID, AND THE CUTOFF OF VENEZUELAN CRUDE (AND PRESSURED MEXICAN SHIPMENTS); DÍAZ-CANEL SAYS CUBA HAS BEEN UNABLE TO IMPORT FUEL SINCE JANUARY EXCEPT ONE RUSSIAN SHIPMENT. IN VENEZUELA, ACTING PRESIDENT DELCY RODRÍGUEZ FACES A DISPUTE THAT HER 180-DAY INTERIM MANDATE HAS LAPSED; MADURO AND CILIA FLORES'S NEXT SDNY HEARING STAYS SET FOR JULY 22 (POSTPONED FROM JUNE 30). NO US GROUND-FORCE MOVES.
daily_entries.summary: Cuba's national electric grid suffered a total collapse at midday on July 6 — the island's third full nationwide blackout in six months (the fourth total outage of 2026) — leaving nearly 10 million people without power; grid operator UNE said it could serve only about 1% of Havana's demand by late afternoon and prioritized hospitals and food-production centers, with restoration underway July 7-8. The failure reflects a de facto US oil blockade, decades of infrastructure decay, and the loss of Venezuelan crude after the Trump administration cut Venezuelan shipments to Cuba and pressured Mexico to halt deliveries; President Díaz-Canel says Cuba has been unable to import fuel since January except for a single Russian shipment. In Venezuela, acting President Delcy Rodríguez — who continues the US-cooperation pattern (oil concessions, detainee releases) — faces a dispute that her 180-day interim mandate has lapsed. Nicolás Maduro and Cilia Flores's next SDNY hearing remains set for July 22, postponed from June 30 over World-Cup-related security logistics. Colombia's transition to Trump-endorsed president-elect Abelardo de la Espriella (handover August 7) continued. No US ground-force moves were reported.

NEW SUPREME LEADER MOJTABA KHAMENEI (NAMED MARCH 9) STILL HAD NOT APPEARED PUBLICLY — REPORTING NOW ATTRIBUTES HIS ABSENCE BOTH TO AN ISRAELI ASSASSINATION THREAT AND TO INJURIES FROM THE FEB 28 STRIKE (US OFFICIALS EARLIER SAID HE WAS 'WOUNDED AND LIKELY DISFIGURED'), KEEPING THE WHO-RUNS-IRAN QUESTION LIVE. US-IRAN TALKS REMAINED PAUSED FOR THE FUNERAL WEEK (TO RESUME 'AT THE EARLIEST POSSIBLE TIME' PER QATAR). BRENT HELD NEAR ITS PRE-WAR ~$72/BBL; HORMUZ FLOWS ABOVE 10M BPD; NO NEW STRIKES OR SHIPPING INCIDENTS REPORTED.
